questions.stem: The SHUNGA dynasty (185-73 BCE) was founded by:
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga — Mauryan commander-in-chief who assassinated the last Mauryan, Brihadratha, in 185 BCE and founded the Shunga dynasty. Ruled from Pataliputra. Agnimitra was his son (and subject of Kalidasa's play Malavikagnimitra). Sanchi Stupa was built/renovated in this period.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The KUSHAN king KANISHKA is remembered for:
questions.explanation: Kanishka (r. ~127-150 CE) — Kushan dynasty. Capital Peshawar (Purushapura). Convened the 4th Buddhist Council in Kashmir — codified Mahayana Buddhism. Started the Saka era (78 CE). Gandhara art + Mathura art flourished under Kushans. patronage of Mahayana.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: Convening the 4th Buddhist Council (Kashmir); patronage of Mahayana

questions.stem: The SATAVAHANA dynasty (ruled in the DECCAN) was founded by:
questions.explanation: Simuka — founder of the Satavahana dynasty c. 230 BCE. Gautamiputra Satakarni (r. ~106-130 CE) was the greatest Satavahana king. Nashik and Karle inscriptions attest his achievements. Hala (~20-24 CE) compiled the Prakrit anthology 'Gaha Sattasai'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The SANGAM AGE of Tamil literature is associated with which dynasties?
questions.explanation: Sangam Age — early centuries CE, three 'Sangams' or academies of Tamil poets in South India. Three kingdoms: Chera (modern Kerala), Chola (Kaveri delta), Pandya (Madurai). Classical Tamil literature: 'Tolkappiyam' (grammar), 'Ettuthokai', 'Pattuppattu', 'Thirukkural' (Tiruvalluvar).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: GANDHARA ART — the famous Indo-Greek-influenced Buddhist sculpture style — flourished under:
questions.explanation: Gandhara region (present NW Pakistan / eastern Afghanistan) — Greco-Roman + Iranian artistic elements fused with Buddhist themes. Earliest Buddha images in anthropomorphic form. Mathura school developed in parallel using Indian idioms. Both Kushan-era; Kanishka a major patron. especially Kanishka.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The CHINESE TRAVELLER who visited India during HARSHA'S reign (7th century CE) was:
questions.explanation: Hiuen Tsang — visited India 629-645 CE during Emperor Harsha's reign. Studied at Nalanda. Wrote 'Xi Yu Ji' ('Record of the Western Regions'). Fa-Hien — earlier (Gupta era, ~400 CE). I-tsing — visited Nalanda later (~675 CE). Megasthenes — Mauryan era.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'CHOLAMANDALAM' (Coromandel coast) of southern India refers to the:

options.option_text: East coast (Bay of Bengal), historically ruled by the Cholas

questions.explanation: 'Coromandel' — English corruption of 'Cholamandalam' ('Realm of the Cholas'). Refers to the east coast of peninsular India. West coast = Malabar (from Cheras of Kerala). Key cities on Coromandel: Chennai, Pondicherry, Thanjavur.
